reason: E2 and E3 support that scanning speed and energy density affect keyholing, balling, and porosity, but no cited evidence directly links dynamic scanning or alternating patterns to reduced thermal gradients, refined microstructure, or improved dimensional accuracy in CoCrFeNiMn. E1 is about a different alloy and process and does not support the specific premises.
premises: Dynamic scanning speed and alternating pattern reduce thermal gradients and melt pool instabilities
Reduced thermal gradients and instabilities lead to refined microstructure and lower porosity
Refined microstructure and lower porosity improve dimensional accuracy and mechanical integrity
Standard SLM of CoCrFeNiMn results in high thermal gradients, porosity, and residual stresses
Keyholing and balling are caused by high energy density and can be mitigated by adjusting scanning parameters
